children: Wall Street closes at 4 p.m. Eastern. Palo Alto Networks, at least one version of it, now doesn't close at all.

MF Markets, a self-custodial perpetual futures platform operated by MANTRA SPC, has listed Palo Alto Networks (PANW) for round-the-clock trading. Anyone with a crypto wallet can access it, and every position is backed by USDC.

The listing lands at a busy moment for the cybersecurity giant. Palo Alto has recently posted strong quarterly numbers and announced a multibillion-dollar AI acquisition, the kind of news that tends to move a stock.
MF Markets pitches itself as a single app for crypto, stocks, indices, commodities, and foreign exchange. Users fund one USDC balance and trade across all of those markets from it.
The platform is self-custodial. Traders connect their own wallets rather than handing assets to a broker, and trades execute onchain against public order books.

The product is a perpetual futures contract, not the stock itself. A perpetual is a derivative that tracks an asset's price without ever expiring. Traders take long or short positions on where the price is heading.
Buying PANW perps on MF Markets doesn't make you a Palo Alto shareholder. You get price exposure, not voting rights or a seat at the annual meeting.

The platform's toolkit includes market-specific leverage limits, take-profit and stop-loss orders, and real-time funding information. Those tools apply across asset classes, so a stock perp behaves much like a crypto perp on the same venue.

Funding is the mechanism that keeps a perpetual's price anchored to the underlying asset. When the contract drifts above or below the reference price, one side of the market pays the other. Real-time visibility into that rate matters, because funding costs can quietly eat into a position held for days.

Palo Alto Networks has given traders plenty to react to lately. On November 18, 2026, the company reported fiscal Q1 2027 revenue of $3.44 billion, a 39% increase from the same quarter a year earlier.
The company also raised its full-year guidance. In addition, it announced a $4.5 billion deal to acquire Applied Compute, an AI startup.

Earnings beats, guidance raises, and big acquisitions share one trait. They often arrive outside regular trading hours, when traditional stock exchanges are closed and most retail traders can only watch.
That gap is the core of MF Markets' pitch. A trader who wants to respond to a late-evening announcement or a weekend headline doesn't have to wait for Monday's opening bell.
The exact timing of the PANW listing relative to the earnings report has not been confirmed.
Palo Alto is the latest addition in a steady expansion. On November 4, 2026, MF Markets launched a futures market tied to New York Harbor ultra-low sulfur diesel.
The single USDC balance is designed so a trader can move from a Bitcoin position to an energy contract to a tech stock without shuffling funds between accounts or brokers.
For individual traders, the obvious benefit is access. Someone in a time zone far from New York can trade PANW exposure during their own daytime, rather than staying up for the US session.
That said, off-hours markets can be thinner, which can mean wider spreads and sharper moves. A price printed on a quiet Sunday may not match where the stock opens on Monday.

Leverage adds another layer. Perpetual futures let traders amplify positions, and amplified positions can be liquidated quickly when prices swing. MF Markets' leverage caps are meant to limit that risk, but they don't eliminate it.

Collateral is also worth watching. Every position on the platform runs on USDC. As venues like this expand into stocks and commodities, the stablecoin increasingly functions as a universal margin currency rather than just a parking spot for crypto traders between trades.

For MANTRA SPC, the PANW listing is another data point in an ongoing bet. The thesis is that traders want one balance, one app, and one set of tools across every market, with custody staying in their own hands.

title: MF Markets adds 24/7 perpetual futures trading for Palo Alto Networks
